COURT’S OR JUDGES’S ORDERS
CRLR No. 233 of 2026, CRLR No. 234 of 2026, CRLR No. 236 of 2026
Hon’ble Rakesh Thapliyal, J. 
1. Mr. Saurabh Kumar Pandey, learned counsel for 
the revisionist.
2. Mr. Tumul Nainwal, learned A.G.A. with Mrs. 
Meenakshi Sharma and Mrs. Sweta Badola Dobhal, 
learned Brief Holders for the State.
3. Mr. D.S. Mehta, learned counsel for the respondent.
4. All these criminal revisions are arising out of three 
different complaints moved by the respondent￾complainant under section 138 of N.I. Act. The Trial 
Court convicted the revisionist in all the complaint cases 
and the conviction was also confirmed by the Appellate 
Court.
5. All these revisions as per the office report are well 
within time.
6. Admit.
7. Summon the Trial Court record.
8. It is argued by the learned counsel for the 
revisionist that the total amount of fine is Rs. 25 lakhs in 
respect of three cheques out of which Rs. 11.55 lakhs has 
already been paid by the revisionist to the complainant 
and the remaining amount is about Rs. 13 lakhs. He 
submits that the revisionist is suffering from some 
ailment and, therefore, he wants to pay the remaining 
amount within four months.
9. Learned counsel for the respondent Mr. D.S. Mehta 
have no objection and submits that if the revisionist is 
ready to pay the balance amount and fine within four 
months then in such an eventuality the exemption 
application, which has been moved by the revisionist, can 
be allowed.
10. In such view of the matter, since the revisionist is 
now giving undertaking through his counsel that he will 
pay balance amount within four months the exemption 
application is allowed.
11. List all these revisions on 12.08.2026.
 
 (Rakesh Thapliyal, J.)
 07.04.2026 PR

COURT’S OR JUDGE’S ORDERS
UKHC010052262026
CRLR/233/2026
Rahul Dhiman
--Revisionist
 Versus
State Of Uttarakhand
--Respondent
With
CRLR /234/2026
CRLR/236/2026
Hon'ble Alok Mahra, J.
Mr. Saurabh Kumar Pandey, learned 
counsel for the revisionist.
Mr. S.S. Chauhan, learned Deputy 
Advocate General, assisted by Mr. Vikash 
Uniyal, learned Brief Holder for the State of 
Uttarakhand.
2. All these Criminal Revisions arise out 
of three different complaints filed under 
Section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments 
Act, 1881. The learned Trial Court convicted 
the revisionist in all the complaints, and the 
said judgments of conviction were affirmed 
by the learned Appellate Court. In all the 
three complaints, the learned Trial Court 
sentenced the revisionist to undergo simple 
imprisonment for a period of three months 
and imposed a total fine of ₹25,00,000/- in 
all the complaints. Out of the said amount, 
the revisionist has paid a sum of ₹11.55 
lakh to the complainant. 
3. The revisionist appeared before a 
Coordinate Bench of this Court on 
07.04.2026. On the undertaking given by 
the learned counsel for the revisionist that
the revisionist was ready and willing to pay 
the remaining amount of ₹13,00,000/-
within a period of four months, Court 
allowed the exemption application filed by  the revisionist and exempted him from 
surrendering before the court concerned. 
4. Today, learned counsel for the 
revisionist submitted that despite the lapse 
of the aforesaid period of four months, the 
revisionist has neither complied with the 
undertaking given before this Court nor paid 
the remaining amount of ₹13,00,000/- to 
the complainant. Learned counsel further 
submitted that despite his advice to the 
revisionist to honour the undertaking given 
before the Court, the revisionist has failed to 
do so. 
5. Considering the facts and 
circumstances of the case, the learned 
Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, 
Kashipur, District Udham Singh Nagar, is 
directed to issue non-bailable warrants 
against the revisionist in Complaint Case 
Nos. 823 of 2017, 959 of 2017 and 16 of 
2017, “Deepa Bisht vs. Rahul Dhiman”, and 
ensure compliance of this order forthwith. 
6. List these Criminal Revisions on 
16.09.2026.
7. Registry is directed to communicate 
this order to the concerned Court forthwith. 
(Alok Mahra, J.)
 12-08-2026
SB

Hon'ble Alok Mahra, J.
Mr. Saurabh Kumar Pandey, learned 
counsel for the revisionist through Video 
Confernecing.
2. Mr. Prabhat Kandpal, learned A.G.A. 
for the State.
3. Mr. D.S. Mehta, learned counsel for 
respondent no.2. 
4. Learned counsel for the revisionist 
submits that Miscellaneous Application (IA 
No. 3 of 2026) has been filed seeking 
cancellation of the non-bailable warrants 
issued against the revisionist and further 
seeking reasonable time to make payment 
of the remaining amount payable to 
respondent no.2.
5. Learned counsel for the revisionist 
further submits that a Coordinate Bench of 
this Court, vide order dated 07.04.2026, 
considering the undertaking furnished by 
the revisionist to pay the remaining 
amount of ₹13,00,000/- within a period of 
four months, had allowed the exemption  application and exempted the revisionist 
from surrendering before the Court 
concerned. It is submitted that, owing to 
his ailment and continuous medical 
treatment, the revisionist could not 
arrange the aforesaid amount within the 
stipulated period. He would further submit
that this Court, vide order dated 
12.08.2026, directed the learned 
Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, 
Kashipur, District Udham Singh Nagar, to 
issue non-bailable warrants against the 
revisionist and fixed the matter for 
16.09.2026.
6. Learned counsel for the revisionist 
submits that the revisionist has, in the 
meantime, made sincere efforts to arrange 
the requisite funds and has paid a sum of 
₹3,00,000/- to respondent no.2 during the 
month of August, 2026, through UPI mode. 
It is submitted that an amount of 
₹10,00,000/- still remains payable to 
respondent no.2. Learned counsel submits 
that the revisionist requires further time of 
two and a half months to arrange the 
remaining amount and undertakes to pay 
the entire outstanding amount within the 
time so granted by this Court.
7. Learned counsel appearing for 
respondent no.2 would submit that the 
revisionist has failed to comply with the 
undertaking earlier given before this Court 
and has not paid the entire amount within 
the stipulated period. However, considering 
the submissions made on behalf of the 
revisionist, learned counsel submits that 
the remaining amount of ₹10,00,000/-
may be directed to be paid in two 
instalments within a specified period.
8. Having considered the submissions 
advanced by learned counsel for the 
parties and taking into account the  payment of ₹3,00,000/- already made by 
the revisionist, this Court is inclined to 
grant one final opportunity to the 
revisionist to clear the remaining amount 
of ₹10,00,000/- payable to respondent 
no.2.
9. Accordingly, the revisionist is directed 
to pay the aforesaid remaining amount of 
₹10,00,000/- to respondent no.2 in two 
equal installments of ₹5,00,000/- each. 
The first installment of ₹5,00,000/- shall 
be paid within a period of 45 days from 
today, and the remaining installment of 
₹5,00,000/- shall be paid within a further 
period of 45 days thereafter.
10. Subject to the revisionist duly 
complying with all the aforesaid conditions 
within the stipulated time, the non-bailable 
warrants issued against him shall remain 
cancelled.
11. It is made clear that the aforesaid 
indulgence is being granted to the 
revisionist as a final opportunity. In the 
event of failure on the part of the 
revisionist to comply with any of the
conditions stipulated hereinabove, or in 
the event of default in making payment of 
either of the instalments within the time 
prescribed, the benefit of cancellation of 
the non-bailable warrants granted by this 
order shall stand automatically vacated, 
and the order dated 12.08.2026, whereby 
non-bailable warrants were issued against 
the revisionist, shall revive and become 
operative without any further order of this 
Court.
12. List this matter on 30.10.2026.
 (Alok Mahra, J.) 07.09.2026 Mamta
